context.projectOverview: Make PgeEngine able to execute a realistic plan at all — today every channel caps at 4,096 bytes while this repository's own PlanSpec is 29,247, so plan_materialize's writes are silently dropped and the run proceeds with state.spec null. Then give the engine a way to report that a run did not do what it claims: a fail-closed refusal of the git-effect commit node currently returns success: true because PipelineResult has no error channel.

completedSprints.title: Observe what a real 29 KB plan actually does to the graph engine
completedSprints.summary: All 6 required criteria met on iteration 1. Harness drives a real PgeEngine over the committed coding.json (all 10 channels confirmed at 4096, not the golden-graph fixture's 8192/65536) and captures the interpreter's GraphRunResult through the interpreterFactory seam that PgeEngine.run discards. MEASURED: spec 29,214 canonical bytes and sprintContracts 135,106 both REJECTED at superstep 12 by plan_materialize against limit 4096; terminal node graceful_failure; status completed / verdict failed; commit.finalize throws FinalizeWithoutSpecError. sc-1-5 fired: spec assumptions[5] corrected 138,284 -> 135,106 (canonicalJson vs naive JSON.stringify); the measurement was committed unchanged. Suite 6856 -> 6860, zero regressions.

completedSprints.title: A committed workload corpus, and the measurement extended to every channel
completedSprints.summary: All 6 required criteria met on iteration 1. Corpus of 123 entries at .bober/workload/ (tracked, nothing leaked into .bober/golden/). byteSize EXPORTED from commit.ts and imported by the corpus helper; sprint 1's duplicate deleted. MEASURED corpus maxima (canonical bytes): spec 48,097 | sprintContracts 135,106 | messages 1,292 | evaluations 1,067 | refs 283 | ledger 221 | testAnchors 114 | branchStatus 102 | counters 64 | verdict 8 — ONLY spec and sprintContracts exceed the 4,096 cap. 60/250 contracts and 1/53 specs fail schema and are skipped by safeParse, deliberately and visibly. refs/counters/branchStatus/ledger have no committed payload and were sourced by OBSERVING a real run through a RunContext.commit spy, provenance {kind:'observed'}. Suite 6860 -> 6871.

completedSprints.title: Size the caps to the corpus, regenerate the artifact, pin both directions
completedSprints.summary: All 7 criteria met on iteration 2. spec 4,096 -> 131,072 and sprintContracts 4,096 -> 524,288; other eight unchanged. graphVersion 1.3.0 + changelog. Caps pinned as EQUALITY to capForCorpusMax = next power of two at or above 2x corpus max — proven non-tautological by the evaluator's own standalone mutation script in both directions for both channels. StateBloatError re-sized, not removed. 5 golden replay cases recaptured, diff verified as exactly graph.graphVersion and nothing else. In-flight specs excluded from the corpus (keyed on PlanSpecStatus) after the corpus was found to invalidate itself mid-run. Suite 6877/0 failed. MAJOR FINDING carried to sprint 4: with the caps raised the run now reaches the 14-contract fan-out and throws SuperstepLimitExceededError at DEFAULT_MAX_SUPERSTEPS=200 before any terminal node. The byte cap was masking a second wall; the two defects only looked like one symptom.

completedSprints.title: Diagnose why a real plan still does not terminate, and fix it only if the cause is a ceiling
completedSprints.summary: 8 of 9 criteria met, 1 skipped by its own mutually-exclusive trigger (sc-4-6 applies only to verdict b). VERDICT: (a) INSUFFICIENT CEILING, independently re-derived by the evaluator at FIVE contract counts — 1:39, 4:84, 7:129, 10:174, 14:234 supersteps — exactly 15 supersteps marginal per contract at every interval. The evaluator also read the raw trace to confirm sprint_body's 1,272 spans are 14 status-ok executions plus 1,258 status-serialized deferral records under concurrency 1 on a real dependsOn DAG, falsifying non-convergence. Fix: PGE_ENGINE_MAX_SUPERSTEPS = supersepsForMeasuredCost(234) = 512, wired into PgeEngine.run's RunContext and pinned two-directionally (a hand-edited literal breaks it; lowering to 200 reproduces the original throw). The interpreter's own DEFAULT_MAX_SUPERSTEPS=200 and throw site were NOT touched. MILESTONE: PgeEngine now executes this repository's own real 29 KB PlanSpec and its 14 real contracts END TO END, terminating at graceful_failure — explicitly not finalize, because commit remains FAIL_CLOSED-refused under the autopilot noop mechanism. No topology change (pge diff empty, graphVersion still 1.3.0). Suite 6877 -> 6879.

completedSprints.title: PipelineResult gains an error channel, layered in the engine
completedSprints.summary: All 9 criteria met on iteration 1. errors?: readonly PipelineFailure[] added to PipelineResult as a PURE TYPE and layered in PgeEngine.run via a CONDITIONAL spread after commit.finalize returns — finalize.ts and finalize.test.ts hash-verified byte-identical before and after. A clean run carries no errors KEY at all (proven with `in`, not an undefined check). success keeps deriveRunSuccess (Option A). All five replay cases re-captured: 52 insertions, ZERO deletions, every added key inside a new errors array and no superstep field — the 1:1-minus-superstep mapping visible in the data. Golden regression 0/5 -> 5/5. Conformance divergence set UNCHANGED at [audits,contracts,history,pipelineResult] with equivalent:false; oracle-retention unmodified. Topology checksum unmoved (sha256:e4909da6...45a5) despite the comment fixes. Suite 6879 -> 6883. NOTE: the curator predicted 4 of 5 cases affected; the fifth (replay-full-run-evaluation-fails) also gained errors, from three LoopExhausted TaskFailures rather than a FailClosed refusal — judged in scope because the layering is generic over any non-empty result.failures, not scoped to one errorClass.

completedSprints.title: An operator can see the refusal
completedSprints.summary: All 5 criteria met on iteration 1. `bober run` sets exitCode 1 and prints a 'Refused:' block naming each failure's nodeId and errorClass; the MCP run manager sets RunState.status='failed' and populates .error, with no schema change. Strictly additive: all four exitCode sites only ever WRITE 1 and never reset, and no path sets status='completed' after the new branch. The evaluator drove a genuinely unmocked PgeEngine to a live commit/FailClosed refusal and fed that real object through the actual runRunCommand and RunManager.startRun paths — exit 1, 'Refused: x commit (FailClosed)', status failed, error populated, persisted to disk, RunState key set unchanged. Suite 6883 -> 6894.

completedSprints.title: A plan that never settles reports failure instead of crashing
completedSprints.summary: All 7 criteria met on iteration 1. New scalar specDraft channel (sole writer plan_draft, cap 65,536 derived by capForCorpusMax from a measured 29,214-byte corpus entry), graphVersion 1.4.0, 11 channels, OverallState 15 -> 16 keys. commit.finalize falls back to specDraft and RESOLVES with success:false + needsClarification:true; FinalizeWithoutSpecError narrowed, not deleted — the evaluator mutated commit.ts in BOTH directions to prove each branch's test genuinely bites. New golden case replay-plan-clarify-rounds-exhausted with exactly 3 plan_draft calls, matching planClarifyRounds maxIterations 3. Five cases recaptured, diffs confined to graphVersion. Golden 6/6. Suite 6894 -> 6897. NOTABLE: the generator first sized specDraft at 131,072 by analogy — sprint 3's equality pin REJECTED it — then at the 4,096 default, which reproduced the exact defect sprint 3 had fixed. It resolved this by adding a measured corpus entry and letting capForCorpusMax derive the value. The two-directional pin did precisely the job it was built for. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: three gate tests were modified because the replay count grew 5 -> 6. Evaluator verdict STRENGTHENED — it reverted each to its pre-sprint logic and confirmed the old versions produced FALSE PASSES against the 6-case dataset, so the changes were a required fix rather than a threshold accommodation.

contract.title: Reconcile the golden dataset, deliberately and diff-first
contract.description: The replay RE-CAPTURE this sprint was written to do already happened — sprint 5 recaptured for the errors key and sprint 7 recaptured again for the 1.4.0 stamp, each with its diff verified. What remains is the work a capture can never do: two hand-authored integrity cases now assert things the runtime has made FALSE, and they must be RE-AUTHORED by judgement. Plus the executor's throws-expectation, which sprint 7 made obsolete, and a negative control that will silently stop biting as the dataset grows.

successCriteria.description: pipeline-result-reports-success-with-no-error-channel.json is RE-AUTHORED. Its caseId, title ('PipelineResult reports success and cannot report why not') and intent ('has NO error channel') are now false — PipelineResult gained errors in sprint 5. A re-capture cannot fix a hand-authored case: replaying a partial pin set throws MissingRecordingError. The prose must be rewritten to state what is true now, and if the caseId itself asserts the falsehood, the case must be renamed (which means a new file and deleting the old one).
commit-refused-fail-closed-under-noop-gate.json is RE-AUTHORED to state what a fail-closed refusal now produces, including the errors array and the exit-code/RunState consequences sprint 6 added.

src/pge/golden/executor.test.ts's expectation that a truncated run THROWS is re-expressed as 'the case does not pass' — sprint 7 made the spec-less path RESOLVE, so a test still asserting a throw is asserting removed behaviour.

executor.test.ts's negative control is made to scale with the dataset. Its 2-of-n mutation currently claims safety 'regardless of how many more cases the replay set grows to hold', which is false: (n-2)/n crosses the 80% threshold at n=11. Either adopt the modulo strategy its two siblings (dataset.test.ts, gate.test.ts) already use, or state the real breakpoint. The control must still be proven to bite by mutation.

The replay count stays at or above GOLDEN_MIN_REPLAY_CASES and no case anywhere is relabelled from replay to integrity. The integrity/replay split is verified by reading the files, not by trusting a count.
The blocking golden regression job passes end to end, both halves, against the reconciled dataset.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green.

nonGoals: Re-capturing replay cases — already done by sprints 5 and 7, with both diffs verified. Do not recapture again unless a criterion here forces it, and say why if it does.
Relabelling any case from replay to integrity to make a count work.
Touching the coverage rule — that is sprint 9.
Changing runtime behaviour of any kind. This sprint reconciles the dataset and its tests to the runtime that already shipped.
stopConditions: Re-authoring a case would require asserting something you cannot verify against the shipped runtime — stop and report.
The dataset drops below the replay floor.
Making sc-8-3 or sc-8-4 pass would require weakening what the test catches — stop; NFR0 forbids it.
contract.definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and every documentation claim added is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
assumptions: VERIFIED: sprint 5 recaptured all five replay cases for the errors key (52 insertions, 0 deletions). Sprint 7 recaptured again for the 1.4.0 graphVersion stamp and added a sixth case. The golden gate is currently 6/6.

The distinction that IS this sprint: a replay case's expectation is CAPTURED from a real run, so a behaviour change legitimately rewrites it. An integrity case is hand-authored prose plus a PARTIAL pin set — replaying one throws MissingRecordingError at the first unpinned call, so it cannot be re-captured at all. Its prose must be rewritten by an act of judgement.

EVALUATOR FINDING carried from sprint 7 (medium): executor.test.ts's fixed 2-case mutation will silently stop biting at n=11 replay cases. Its siblings dataset.test.ts and gate.test.ts already switched to a scaling modulo strategy.

DOCUMENTER FINDING carried from sprint 5: the first case's own FILENAME and caseId assert the falsehood ('pipeline-result-reports-success-with-no-error-channel'). Renaming means a new file plus deleting the old one — a caseId that contradicts the runtime is worse than a stale comment, because the dataset validity check ties caseId to filename.
contract.generatorNotes: The distinction between re-CAPTURE and re-AUTHOR is the whole sprint. A replay case's expectation is captured from a real run, so a behaviour change legitimately rewrites it. An integrity case is hand-authored prose plus a partial pin set: when the behaviour it describes changes, the PROSE is now false and must be rewritten by a human-equivalent act of judgement -- re-capturing it is not even possible, since replaying a partial pin set throws MissingRecordingError at the first unpinned call. Read the two named files and rewrite what they claim. When you re-capture the five, read the resulting diff before committing and write down what moved.
contract.evaluatorNotes: This sprint is where a green gate is least trustworthy, so verify the diff yourself. For each re-captured case, check the change is confined to the error channel and its consequences -- an unrelated artifact that moved is a finding. For the two re-authored cases, read their prose and confirm it describes current behaviour; a case that still claims PipelineResult has no error channel fails sc-8-2 regardless of whether the suite is green. Confirm the replay count by counting files with enforcement replay yourself. Confirm sc-8-5 by reading the rewritten assertion -- 'does not pass' and 'throws' are different claims and only one is now true.

principles:
# Project Principles

> These principles guide all planning, generation, and evaluation in the Bober pipeline.
> Updated: 2026-04-16

## Mission

Agent-bober is a multi-agent harness that builds applications autonomously using any LLM. It orchestrates a pipeline of specialized agents (Researcher, Planner, Curator, Generator, Evaluator) and supports Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Ollama. It ships as an npm CLI + MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf.

## Users

- **Primary:** Developers using Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf who want autonomous feature generation with quality gates
- **Secondary:** Teams integrating agent-bober programmatically via the TypeScript API or MCP server
- Technical level: intermediate to advanced — users understand LLMs, CI/CD, and modern JS tooling

## Quality Standards

- **Type safety:** TypeScript strict mode with all strict flags (`noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `isolatedModules`). Zero type errors is a hard gate.
- **Lint compliance:** ESLint flat config with `consistent-type-imports` enforced, `no-explicit-any` warned, unused vars errored (with `_` prefix escape). Zero lint errors is a hard gate.
- **Test coverage:** Vitest for unit tests. Tests are collocated with source (`*.test.ts` next to `*.ts`). Tests run against the real project when practical (e.g., scanner tests scan agent-bober itself).
- **Build integrity:** `tsc` must produce clean output. Build is a required evaluator strategy.

## Technical Principles

### Follow

- **ESM everywhere.** `"type": "module"` in package.json. All imports use `.js` extensions for NodeNext resolution. No CommonJS.
- **Provider-agnostic interfaces.** All LLM interaction goes through `providers/types.ts` — provider-specific SDKs are wrapped by adapters (`anthropic.ts`, `openai.ts`, `google.ts`). Never leak SDK types outside adapter files.
- **Zod for config validation.** All configuration schemas are Zod schemas in `config/schema.ts`. Runtime config loading uses `z.parse()`. No hand-rolled validation.
- **Contract-based architecture.** PlanSpecs, SprintContracts, and EvalResults are the communication protocol between agents. They live in `contracts/` and are JSON files on disk in `.bober/`.
- **Filesystem state.** All mutable state (specs, contracts, handoffs, eval results, history) is stored as JSON files in `.bober/`. No database, no in-memory global state.
- **Section comments.** Use unicode box-drawing section headers: `// -- Section Name ------` to organize long files.
- **Small utility modules.** Utils in `utils/` are focused single-purpose files (`fs.ts`, `git.ts`, `logger.ts`). Keep them small.
- **Conventional commits.** Format: `type: description` where type is `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `release`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`. Sprint-generated commits use `bober(sprint-N): description`.
- **Use `type` imports.** ESLint enforces `consistent-type-imports` -- import types with `import type { ... }` syntax.
- **Prefix unused params with `_`.** The `_` prefix is the only escape hatch for unused variables/parameters.

### Avoid

- **No `any` without justification.** `no-explicit-any` is a warning; aim for zero. Use `unknown` + type narrowing instead.
- **No SDK lock-in.** Never import `@anthropic-ai/sdk` or `openai` outside of their respective adapter files in `providers/`.
- **No synchronous filesystem ops.** All fs operations use `node:fs/promises`. No `fs.readFileSync` etc.
- **No barrel re-exports for deep internals.** `src/index.ts` exports the public API only. Internal modules import directly.
- **No test mocks for filesystem.** Tests that need filesystem state create temp directories and clean up. The scanner tests run against the real codebase.

## Design Principles

N/A -- no user interface. Agent-bober is a CLI tool and programmatic library. The MCP server exposes tools, not UI.
